ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r6.claim: God holds every creature's forelock as a figurative image of total ownership and power, like leading a captive or horse; Arabs also shaved a captive's forelock as a sign of control.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r6.anchor: وقوله: آخذ بناصيتها تمثيل، إذ كان القادر المالك يقود المقدور عليه بناصيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the forelock is singled out because Arabs describe someone as humbled by saying his forelock is in another person's hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: وخص الناصية لأن العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r8.claim: God's actions are perfectly ordered and just: no wrongdoer escapes and no one who relies on Him is lost, while His word and promise are true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p168/r8.anchor: ثم أخبر أن أفعاله تعالى في غاية الإحكام، وعلى طريق الحق والعدل في ملكه، لا يفوته ظالم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Hūd's declaration that every living creature is in God's grasp undergirds his challenge; he needs no mediators or intercessors to reach God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They should not think that he has to reach God after passing through various contorted and twisted paths

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The idolaters believed that their deities were a means to bring them to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It may be kept in mind that the idolaters believed that their deities were a means to

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur'an condemns idolaters for blocking God's path and seeking distortions in it; Hūd refutes their baseless mediation theory.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is as a result of this belief that the Qur’ ān points out their crime of stopping people from the path of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: A true monotheist's sense of direct nearness to God gives the trust needed to challenge everyone, as Hūd does.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: unless there exists that concept of God’s nearness which exists in a true monotheist, a person cannot have that trust in God

MAJAZ:v1p289/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r9.claim: Ākhidh bi-nāṣiyatihā means that He holds it in His grasp, ownership, and power.
MAJAZ:v1p289/r9.anchor: «إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها» (56) مجازه إلا هو فى قبضته وملكه وسلطانه.

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r4.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r4.claim: Hūd’s firm reliance on God is the reason he is confident that his opponents cannot scheme against him.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r4.anchor: reason for his confidence in their inability to scheme against him, namely, his firm and unshakeable reliance upon God (Kl)

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r5.speaker: N
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r5.claim: The forelock image metaphorically expresses that all creatures are under God’s control and authority.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r5.anchor: There is no creature that crawls, but that He holds it by its forelock is a metaphor to denote that all creatures are under God’s Control and Authority (N).

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r6.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r6.claim: The straight path means God is on the path of truth, is just, and does not let wrongdoers escape Him.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r6.anchor: Truly my Lord is upon a straight path means that God is upon the path of truth, is Just, and does not let wrongdoers escape Him.

STUDYQURAN:11:55/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r7.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r7.claim: The straight path also means God will not forsake a person who relies upon Him.
STUDYQURAN:11:55/r7.anchor: It also means that He will not forsake one who relies upon Him (Z). Regarding straight path, see 1:6c.

TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r1.claim: Hud entrusts himself to Allah, the owner and governor of him and his people; every creature belongs to Allah, is held in His power, and is submissive to Him.
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r1.anchor: وهو في قبضته وسلطانه ذليل له خاضع

TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r2.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock evokes mastery and subjection: Arabs said a person's forelock was in another's hand and shaved captives' forelocks to boast of their control.
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r2.anchor: قيل: لأن العرب كانت تستعمل ذلك في وصفها من وصفته بالذلة والخضوع، فتقول: ما ناصية فلان إلا بيد فلان

TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r3.claim: Allah is on the path of truth: He rewards good and evil justly, wrongs no one, and accepts only Islam and faith in Him.
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r3.anchor: يقول: إن ربي على طريق الحق، يجازي المحسن من خلقه بإحسانه والمسيء بإساءته، لا يظلم أحدا منهم شيئا

TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses the straight path as the truth.
TAB-FULL:v12p449#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {إن ربي على صراط مستقيم} [هود: 56] الحق "

TABATABAI:2:21-25#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#20/r1.claim: Since the Qur’an affirms universal creation, an ordered creation, and general causality, material events—customary or miraculous—follow a stable order and arise from a preceding cause.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#20/r1.anchor: أن نظام الوجود في الموجودات المادية سواء كانت على جري العادة أو خارقة لها على صراط مستقيم

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r6.claim: Hūd explains that his trust is in God, who directs both his affairs and those of his people, removing any implication that the challenge rests on fearlessness alone.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r6.anchor: فذكر أنه متوكل في أمره على الله الذي هو يدبر أمره وأمرهم

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r7.claim: “Every creature” means every animal that moves on earth; taking it by the forelock is a figure for complete sovereignty and ultimate power.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r7.anchor: والأخذ بالناصية كناية عن كمال السلطة ونهاية القدرة

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r8.claim: God’s being on a straight path means His governance follows one constant, unchanging way of justice and wisdom, vindicating truth when it confronts falsehood.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r8.anchor: وكونه تعالى على صراط مستقيم هو كون سنته في الخليقة واحدة ثابتة غير متغيرة وهو تدبير الأمور على منهاج العدل والحكمة

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r9.claim: Hūd’s trust will succeed: God owns and rules him, his people, and every creature, and His just, constant practice is to support His religion and protect Hūd from their harm.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r9.anchor: فالمعنى أني توكلت على الله ربي وربكم في نجاح حجتي التي ألقيتها إليكم

TABATABAI:11:56-58/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:56-58/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:56-58/r1.claim: Hūd says “my Lord” on the straight path, not “my Lord and your Lord,” because here he seeks protection for himself through his bond of servitude; the earlier wording stated God’s universal rule.
TABATABAI:11:56-58/r1.anchor: فإنه في مقام الدعاء لنفسه على قومه يتوقع أن يحفظه الله من شرهم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.claim: ʿĀd were prehistoric Arab inhabitants of the peninsula; their history survives only in unreliable tales, and the extant Torah does not mention them.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.anchor: عاد قوم هود هؤلاء قوم من العرب من بشر ما قبل التاريخ كانوا يسكنون الجزيرة انقطعت أخبارهم وانمحت آثارهم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.claim: The Quran places ʿĀd after Noah in al-Aḥqāf; the name may be “first ʿĀd,” suggesting a second ʿĀd as well.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.anchor: كانوا قوما يسكنون الأحقاف من شبه جزيرة العرب بعد قوم نوح

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.claim: The people were tall, strong, and physically imposing, with advanced urban life, thriving towns, fertile land, gardens, date palms, and crops.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.anchor: كانت لهم أجساد طويلة وكانوا ذوي بسطة في الخلق أولي قوة وبطش شديد وكان لهم تقدم ورقي في المدينة والحضارة

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.claim: After enjoying God’s bounty, they developed idolatry, built monuments on every rise and grand structures as if to live forever, and obeyed arrogant tyrants.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.anchor: لم يزل القوم يتنعمون بنعمة الله حتى غيروا ما بأنفسهم فتعرقت فيهم الوثنية وبنوا بكل ريع آية يعبثون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.claim: God sent their kinsman Hūd to call them to truth, worship of God, rejection of idols, justice, and mercy; he admonished them and made the way clear.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم أخاهم هودا يدعوهم إلى الحق ويرشدهم إلى أن يعبدوا الله ويرفضوا الأوثان

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.claim: Only a small group believed; most persisted in defiance, called Hūd foolish and mad, and demanded the threatened punishment, to which he replied that its timing belongs to God.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.anchor: وأصر جمهورهم على البغي والعناد، ورموه بالسفه والجنون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.claim: God sent a barren, furious wind through adverse days, lasting seven nights and eight days; it left the people fallen like hollow palm trunks and destroyed them all but their dwellings.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.anchor: وأرسل إليهم الريح العقيم ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.claim: They first mistook the cloud approaching their valleys for rain, but it was the very calamity they had demanded; God annihilated them and saved Hūd and the believers by His mercy.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.anchor: وكانوا بادئ ما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم استبشروا وقالوا عارض ممطرنا وقد أخطأوا بل كان هو الذي استعجلوا به

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.claim: Hūd was from ʿĀd and the second prophet whose struggle against idolatry and suffering for God the Quran narrates; God praises him among the noble messengers.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.anchor: وأما هود عليه السلام فهو من قوم عاد وثاني الأنبياء الذين انتهضوا للدفاع عن الحق ودحض الوثنية ممن ذكر الله قصته وما قاساه

TABRISI:11:50-60/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60/r5.claim: The “nāṣiya” is the forelock; its root connotes connection, as in a desert joining another desert, with cited verse fragments using the root.

TABRISI:11:50-60/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60/r6.speaker: أبو النجم
TABRISI:11:50-60/r6.claim: Abu al-Najm's verse about gray hairs and “al-manāṣī” is cited as evidence for the root's sense of joining or pulling something together.
TABRISI:11:50-60/r6.anchor: وقال أبو النجم: إن يمس رأسي أشمط العناصي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r1.claim: The naṣiya is the hairline at the front of the head.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r1.anchor: قال الليث (¬6): الناصية هي: قصاص الشعر في مقدمة الرأس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra defines the naṣiya as the front of the head.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r3.claim: Among Arabs the naṣiya is the hairline at the forehead; the fixed hair is named for its place, and the verbs describe pulling or tugging one another by the forelock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r3.anchor: قال الأزهري: الناصية عند العرب: منبت الشعر في مقدمة الرأس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r4.speaker: عمرو بن معدي كرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r4.claim: A line by Amr ibn Ma'di Karib uses ناصيت to mean seizing or tugging someone by the forelock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r4.anchor: ومنه قول عمرو بن معدي كرب (¬1): أعباس لو كانت شيارا جيادنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r5.claim: Every creature is in God's grasp, and His power reaches it however He wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى {إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها} أي: هي في قبضته وتنالها بما شاء قدرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r6.claim: Though interpreters phrase it differently, the idiom means creatures are humbled and controlled by God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2)، وهذا معنى هذا الكلام، وإن اختلفت العبارات في تفسيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir explains that holding a person's forelock is an Arabic idiom for obedience and control; shaving a captive's forelock signified the captor's mastery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p447#2/r7.anchor: ما ذكره ابن جرير (¬3) فقال: العرب إذا وصفت إنسانا بالذلة والخضوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r1.claim: Although God can reach them by His power, He wills only justice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬1): أي: هو وإن كانت قدرته تنالهم بما شاء فهو لا يشاء إلا العدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r2.claim: Though every creature is in God's grip, He does not wrong them and only brings on them what justice requires; this is Mujahid's explanation as being upon truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r2.anchor: وزاد ابن الأنباري (¬2) لهذا بيانا فقال: لما قال {إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد {إن ربي على صراط مستقيم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r4.claim: Arab speakers describe someone of good conduct, justice, and beneficence as being on a good path, though no literal path is meant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r4.anchor: وهذا نحو كلام العرب إذا وصفوا رجلا بحسن السيرة والعدل والإحسان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r5.claim: Another explanation is that no hidden person or fugitive can escape God's reach; the straight path is the route no one can avoid, as in 89:14.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r5.anchor: وذكر وجها آخر قال: لما ذكر أن سلطانه قد قهر كل دابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r6.claim: The straight path is the upright religion God sent Hud to teach.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس (¬6) في هذه الآية يريد أن الذي بعثني الله به دين مستقيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r7.claim: The straight path is abiding and enduring, namely Islam, to which God guides whomever He wills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬1): {إن ربي على صراط مستقيم} يقول: قائم دائم، وهو الإسلام والطريق عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r8.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r8.claim: On the interpretation that the path is Islam, some supply an ellipsis: God is on a straight path and urges or leads people to call to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r8.anchor: ولهذا المعنى ذهب بعض أهل المعاني (¬2) إلى إضمار في الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r9.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r9.claim: Others understand an omitted genitive: God's command and governance of creation are on a straight path without flaw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p449/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم (¬4): هذا من باب حذف المضاف؛ على معنى أن أمر ربي

QASHANI:11:52-53/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:52-53/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:52-53/r6.claim: Hud's trust in God rests first on God's universal lordship: a Lord manages and protects every creature, so no other guardian is needed.
QASHANI:11:52-53/r6.anchor: بين وجوب التوكل على الله وكونه حصنا حصينا أولا بأن ربوبيته شاملة لكل أحد

QASHANI:11:52-53/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:52-53/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:52-53/r7.claim: Every creature is captive under God's power and cannot independently act or affect another, so there is no need to guard against it.
QASHANI:11:52-53/r7.anchor: ثم بان كل ذي نفس تحت قهره وسلطانه أسير في يد تصرفه ومملكته وقدرته عاجز عن الفعل والقوة

QASHANI:11:52-53/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:52-53/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:52-53/r8.claim: God's straight path is justice amid multiplicity, a shadow of unity: authority is imposed only on those who deserve it through fault, and punishment follows a lapse, sometimes purifying or raising rank as martyrdom does.
QASHANI:11:52-53/r8.anchor: على طريق العدل في عالم الكثرة الذي هو ظل وحدته فلا يسلط أحدا على أحد إلا عن استحقاق

QASHANI:11:52-53/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:52-53/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:52-53/r9.claim: These claims together deny independent power to benefit or harm both people and their idols.
QASHANI:11:52-53/r9.anchor: وفي ضمن ذلك كله نفي القدرة على النفع والضر عنهم وعن آلهتهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r1.claim: Every creature is in God's grasp and subject to whatever His power wills for it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r1.anchor: أي: هي في قبضته، وتنالها بما شاء قدرته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r2.claim: The religion God sent Hud with is a straight religion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:56-58/r2.anchor: إن الذي بعثني الله به دين مستقيم

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r7.claim: Hud relies on God's command and protection: God is lord and master of both Hud and his people, so nothing they do or any harm that reaches him occurs apart from God's will.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r7.anchor: Ben her hâlde Allah’a tevekkül ettim O’nun emr ü hıfzına dayandım {رَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم} ki Rabbim ve Rabbinizdir. Benim de mâlikim, efendim O’dur sizin de.

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r8.claim: Every moving creature is in God's grasp and power, owned and subdued by Him; taking it by the forelock is an idiom for control and subjugation, and none escapes His disposal.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r8.anchor: Nâsıyesinden tutmak, perçeminden yakalamak, zabt u teshirde[^3] meseldir.

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r9.claim: God is on a straight path in the sense that He upholds truth and helps the truthful; His pleasure lies with truth, justice, and uprightness.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r9.anchor: Doğruluğun hâmîsi, doğruların yardımcısıdır. Rızâsı hakk u adl ve istikāmettedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r6.claim: Every living creature is under God's command and control, with his power and will absolute over all beings; Hud trusts that none can harm him without God's leave.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r6.anchor: Hûd bu sözüyle Allah’ın izni olmadan kendisine kimsenin tuzak kurup kötülük yapamayacağına inancının tam olduğunu vurgulamak istemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r7.claim: The literal rendering is “my Lord is upon a straight path”; this means God's judgments and acts are wholly right and just, free from injustice, error, and wrongdoing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r7.anchor: Allah’ın yolunun dosdoğru yol olmasından maksat, O’nun hüküm ve tasarruflarının tamamen doğru, adalete uygun olması

SULAMI:v1p320/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p320/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p320/r5.claim: One reflection asks how anyone can claim independent standing when existence depends on another, and says that whoever says I contests God's grip.
SULAMI:v1p320/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : كيف يكون ذلك محل وأنت بغيرك قيامك

SULAMI:v1p320/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p320/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p320/r6.claim: Another reflection says the verse invalidates self-claims: whoever asserts a claim wages war on divine power and contests God's grasp.
SULAMI:v1p320/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : فيه ذكر إبطال الدعاوى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p115/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p115/r2.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock means subduing and humiliating it through sovereign power; ناصيتي بيدك likewise means You own and overpower me.

NAHHAS:v2p287/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p287/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p287/r6.claim: Tawakkaltu means Hud accepted God's judgment and trusted His help.

NAHHAS:v2p287/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p287/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p287/r7.claim: ما من دابة is a subject, with إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها as its predicate; God directs every creature, so Hud's opponents cannot harm him.
NAHHAS:v2p287/r7.anchor: ( ما من دابة ) في موضع رفع بالابتداء ( إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها ) أي يصرفها كيف يشاء

NAHHAS:v2p287/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p287/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p287/r8.claim: Any living thing is called a dābb or dābba; the feminine ending intensifies the form.
NAHHAS:v2p287/r8.anchor: وكل ما فيه الروح يقال له داب ودابة والهاء للمبالغة

NAHHAS:v2p287/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p287/r9.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p287/r9.claim: One explanation is that God's governance has no flaw and His creation no disparity.
NAHHAS:v2p287/r9.anchor: قيل معناه لا خلل في تدبيره ولا تفاوت في خلقه

SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r1.claim: The nāṣiya is the hairline at the front of the head; by extension, the hair growing there is also called a nāṣiya after its place.
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r1.anchor: والناصية منبت الشعر في مقدم الرأس، ويسمى الشعر النابت أيضا " ناصية " باسم محله

SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r2.claim: نصوت الرجل means I seized the man by his forelock, showing a wāw as the root's final radical; ناصاة is also said, with its yāʾ changed to alif.
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r2.anchor: ونصوت الرجل: أخذت بناصيته، فلامها واو، ويقال: ناصاة بقلب يائها ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r3.claim: Taking someone by the forelock signifies mastery and control even without literal seizure; masters showed favor to captives by shaving their forelocks.
SAMIN-DURR:11:56/r3.anchor: وفي الأخذ بالناصية عبارة عن الغلبة والتسلط وإن لم يكن آخذا بناصيته

ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r3.claim: Every creature is in God's grasp, and His power can bring it under whatever action He wills.

ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r4.claim: Although God's power reaches creatures as He wills, He wills only what is just.
ZAJJAJ:v3p58/r4.anchor: أي هو سبحانه وإن كانت قدرته تنالها

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r1.claim: Being held by the forelock means that every living being is fully controlled by God and depends entirely on Him.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r1.anchor: there is no living being over which He has not complete control and which is not entirely dependent on Him

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r2.claim: Ancient Arabs used the forelock-in-another's-hand idiom for a person's humility and subjection.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r2.anchor: the ancient Arabs used to say, "The forelock of so-and-so is in the hand of so-and-so"

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r3.claim: Asad connects the expression with 11:6, where he has discussed God's control over living beings.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r3.anchor: complete control and which is not entirely dependent on Him (cf. verse 6 of this surah)

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r4.claim: The same idiom occurs in 96:15-16, its first occurrence in chronological revelation order.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n80/r4.anchor: 96:15-16, where this idiomatic expression occurs for the first time in the chronological order of Qur'anic revelation

ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n81/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n81/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n81/r1.claim: God governs by ultimate truth and justice, ensures evildoers face consequences and righteousness is rewarded in this world and the hereafter.
ASAD-NOTES:11:53#n81/r1.anchor: He governs all that exists in accordance with a system of truth and justice in the ultimate, absolute sense of these terms

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.claim: Hud repeatedly uses the first-person yā in this passage, whereas Araf shows it only once, in “Indeed, my protector is Allah”; this repetition suits Hud.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#2/r5.anchor: ومن ناحية أخرى نرى أنه قد تردد ذكر ياء الضمير في هود في هذا الموطن مرات عديدة

QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#1/r1.speaker: Qunbul/Ruways
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#1/r1.claim: The sin reading for ṣād is attributed to Qunbul and Ruways; both forms trace to the same Semitic root for road.
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#1/r1.anchor: sin replaces ṣād — Qunbul/Ruways reading; both ṣirāṭ and sirāṭ trace t

QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#2/r1.speaker: Khalaf ʿan Ḥamza
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#2/r1.claim: Khalaf from Ḥamza uses ishmām, coloring ṣād slightly with zāy to produce an intermediate sound between ṣ and s.
QIRAAT-ER:11:56:19#2/r1.anchor: ishmām: ṣād pronounced with a slight zāy coloring — Khalaf ʿan Ḥamza; a phonetic intermediate between ṣ and s

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r1.claim: His reliance explains why their combined effort cannot harm him: God owns both him and them, and nothing occurs except by God's will.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r1.anchor: يعني أنكم وإن لم تبقوا في القوس منزعا وبذلتم مضادتي مجهودكم لا تقدرون على شيء مما تريدون بي فإني متوكل على الله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r2.claim: The past tense is chosen because it better conveys a performative commitment suited to the moment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r2.anchor: وجيء بلفظ الماضي لأنه أدل على الإنشاء المناسب للمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r3.claim: Every living creature is under God's ownership and power, directed as He wills and unable to resist Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r3.anchor: أي إلا هو مالك لها قادر عليها يصرفها كيف يشاء غير مستعصية عليه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r4.claim: The nāṣiya is the front of the head, including the hair growing there.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r4.anchor: والناصية مقدم الرأس وتطلق على الشعر النابت عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r5.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock is a metaphor or metonym for mastery; Arabs shaved a captive's forelock to mark that he had been seized.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r5.anchor: واستعمال الأخذ بالناصية في القدرة والتسلط مجاز أو كناية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r6.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r6.claim: Al-Baḥr says the expression had become a conventional idiom for power over an animal.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r6.anchor: وفي البحر أنه صار عرفا في القدرة على الحيوان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r7.claim: The straight path is a representation: God watches over creatures, judges them with reward or punishment, and protects whoever takes refuge in Him, like a guardian on a road.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r7.anchor: وهو تمثيل واستعارة لأنه تعالى مطلع على أمور العباد مجاز لهم بالثواب والعقاب كاف لمن اعتصم به

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r8.claim: He links the assurance to God's watchfulness in 89:14, “Your Lord is ever watchful.”
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r8.anchor: إليه تعالى للجزاء وفصل القضاء ولعل الأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r9.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r9.claim: Al-Kashf notes the progression: reliance removes fear, naming God as Lord of both sides heightens the challenge, and universal control of creatures seals the proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r9.anchor: من حسن التعليل وما يعطيه أن من توكل عليه لم يبال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r10.claim: Calling God “my Lord” without repeating “your Lord” intimates special care for Hūd, while affirming that God is Lord of all by right.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p83#2/r10.anchor: كما في الأول نكتة سرية بعد اختصار المعنى عن الحشو فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.claim: Hūd's reliance means that he depends on God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r4.anchor: {إني توكلت} أي: اعتمدت {على الله ربي وربكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets God's taking every creature by its forelock as giving it life and death.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains that God owns every creature and has power over it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.speaker: القُتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybī reads the image as subjugation, since one whose forelock is held has been overpowered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r7.anchor: وقال القتيبي: يقهرها، لأن من أخذت بناصيته فقد قهرته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.claim: The forelock is singled out because Arabs used its possession to signify humiliation: captors cut the forelocks of released prisoners as a boast over them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: إنما خص الناصية بالذكر لأن العرب تستعمل ذلك إذا وصفت إنسانا بالذلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.claim: Although God has power over them, He does not wrong them and acts only with goodness and justice, rewarding good and punishing evil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r9.anchor: إن ربي وإن كان قادرا عليهم فإنه لا يظلمهم ولا يعمل إلا بالإحسان والعدل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r10.claim: Another explanation is that God's religion leads to a straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن دين ربي إلى صراط مستقيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r11.claim: An ellipsis is proposed: God urges and carries them onto a straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183#2/r11.anchor: وقيل (1) فيه إضمار، أي: إن ربي يحثكم ويحملكم على صراط مستقيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r1.claim: Hud trusts God’s protection: God owns both Hud and them, so they cannot harm him except by what God wills or decrees.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r1.anchor: أنكم وإن بذلتم غاية وسعكم لن تضروني

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r2.claim: God owns every creature and can direct it as He wills; taking a creature by its forelock is a metaphor for this control.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r2.anchor: إلا وهو مالك لها قادر عليها يصرفها على ما يريد بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r3.claim: God is just and true: no one who seeks refuge with Him is lost, and no wrongdoer escapes Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:56/r3.anchor: على الحق والعدل لا يضيع عنده معتصم ولا يفوته ظالم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r10.claim: The implied challenge is that Hūd is alone against their numbers and strength; he answers that he relies on God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r10.anchor: فما حملك على الاجتراء على مخالفتنا نحن وأنت كثرتنا وقوتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r11.claim: Tawakkul means relying on God, the feared sovereign, who alone is king and Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r11.anchor: { إني } أي جسرت على ذلك لأني { توكلت } معتمدا { على الله } الملك المرهوب عقابه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r12.claim: God is Lord of both because He created them and directed their affairs before their creation, knowing what each would do for the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r12.anchor: { ربي وربكم } أي الذي أوجدنا ودبر أمورنا قبل أن يخلقنا فعلم ما بعمل كل منا في حق الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r13.claim: God has power and mastery over every creature, small or large, by taking it in a grip of force and conquest.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r13.anchor: { ما من دابة } أس صغرت أو كبرت { إلا هو آخذ } أي أخذ قهر وغلبة { بناصيتها }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r14.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head; being seized by it means submitting to God's control and being unable to turn aside.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r14.anchor: ومن أخذ بناصيته فقد انقاد لأخذه لا يستطيع ميلا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r15.claim: The word nāṣiya is connected etymologically with joining, as in two contiguous deserts described as tanāṣā.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r15.anchor: والناصية : مقدم الشعر من الرأس , وأصلها الاتصال من قولهم : مفازة تناصي مفازة - إذا كانت متصلة بها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r16.claim: Biqāʿī explains inna causally here: because his Lord, who has sustained him, is upon a broad and clear road.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r16.anchor: { إن } أي لأن { ربي } أي المحسن إلي بما أقامني فيه { على الصراط } أي طريق واسع بين { مستقيم * }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r17.claim: The straight path is manifest, broad, and free of ambiguity, defect, disorder, or deviation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r17.anchor: ظاهر أمره لكل أحد لا لبس فيه أصلا ولا خلل ولا اضطراب ولا اعوجاج بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r18.claim: All beings worship, call upon, fear, and hope in God, even when some associate partners; only the worshippers honor idols, while others disregard them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r18.anchor: فلذلك كان كل من في الكون يتألهه ويدعو ويخافه ويرجوه وإن اتخذ بعضهم من دونه شركاء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r19.claim: Because the path is clear, its adherents know their purpose and remain firm, feared, followed, and loved; those who reject it go astray, and those who turn away are seized.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r19.anchor: فمن كان عليه كان علي القدر شهير الأمر , بصيرا بما يريد , مع الثبات والتمكن , مرهوب العاقبة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r20.claim: Since every forelock is in God's hand, He can protect those who rely on Him while their gods are powerless; He is Lord of idols, worshippers, and all things.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r20.anchor: فظهرت قدرته على عصمة من يتوكل عليه وعجز معبوداتهم معهمن لأن نواصي الكل بيده وهو ربها وربهم ورب كل شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r21.claim: The ending answers their claim that Hūd brought no proof: nothing is clearer than the affair of one whose Lord is on a straight path (11:53).
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r21.anchor: فقد انطبقختام الآية على قولهم { ما جئتنا ببينة } ردا له لأن من كان على صراط مستقيم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r22.claim: The close also fits Hūd's answer about reliance and God's comprehensive control.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p543/r22.anchor: وعلى جوابه في توكله وما في حيزه أتك انطباق

DURR-FULL:v4p443/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Saʿid reports that reciting this verse against a robber, predator, or rebellious devil leads God to turn it away.
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن سعيد قال: ما من أحد يخاف لصا عاديا أو سبعا ضاريا أو شيطانا ماردا فيتلو

DURR-FULL:v4p443/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses God being on a straight path as the truth.
DURR-FULL:v4p443/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {إن ربي على صراط مستقيم} قال: الحق

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r1.speaker: يفع بن عبد الكلاعي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r1.claim: Yaf ibn Abd al-Kalai says God controls His servants, treating the believer more gently than a parent treats a child and confronting the disbeliever with the question of what deceived him about his gracious Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r1.anchor: عن يفع بن عبد الكلاعي انه قال في قوله : مامن دابة الا هو اخذ بناصيتها ان ربي على صراط مستقيم قال

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r2.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r2.claim: The commentary notes that it has already explained the straight path several times.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2047/r2.anchor: قد تقدم تفسير الصراط المستقيم غير مرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r5.claim: Reliance on God explains the challenge: Hud is confident the people cannot harm him because he trusts in God, an old religious principle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r5.anchor: وهو التعجيز والاحتقار . يعني : أنه واثق بعجزهم عن كيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r6.claim: Calling God the Lord of both Hud and his opponents grounds reliance in God's ownership of all of them and power to protect some from others' injustice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r6.anchor: لأنه مالكهم جميعا يدفع ظلم بعضهم بعضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r7.claim: The clause about every creature being held by its forelock may be an adjective of God's name or a circumstantial clause; either serves the same purpose as the lordship description.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r7.anchor: في محل صفة لاسم الجلالة ، أو حال منه ، والغرض منها مثل الغرض من صفة الربوبية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r8.claim: Taking means grasping; the forelock is the hair falling over the forehead, and grasping it pictures control like holding a person's head so he cannot escape.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r8.anchor: والأخذ : الإمساك . والناصية : ما انسدل على الجبهة من شعر الرأس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r9.claim: The image is figurative because many creatures lack forelocks; it means God governs all, especially humans, and as owner and conqueror cannot be escaped or overcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p99/r9.anchor: ومن بديع هذا المثل أنه أشد اختصاصا بالنوع المقصود من بين عموم الدواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r1.claim: على is a metaphor of elevation for steadfast moral establishment, comparable to the believers being upon guidance in 2:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r1.anchor: مستعارة للتمكن المعنوي ، وهو الاتصاف الراسخ الذي لا يتغير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r2.claim: The straight path is a metaphor for actions conforming to justice and wisdom; justice resembles straightness and evenness, as in 19:43.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r2.anchor: مستعار للفعل الجاري على مقتضى العدل والحكمة لأن العدل يشبه بالاستقامة والسواء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r3.claim: This clause explains reliance: God merits trust because He acts justly and supports His messengers, so He does not hand one who trusts Him over to wrongdoers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p101/r3.anchor: وجملة { إن ربي على صراط مستقيم } تعليل لجملة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r8.claim: Hūd’s trust in the Lord of both parties protects him despite his weakness and isolation against their strength and numbers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r8.anchor: المعنى: أن توكلي على الله الذي هو ربي وربكم مع ضعفي وانفرادي وقوتكم وكثرتكم يمنعني منكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r9.claim: Taking every creature by its forelock describes God’s power and mastery; the forelock is where a captor holds someone under his control.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r9.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك ب «الناصية» ، إذ هي في العرف حيث يقبض القادر المالك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r10.claim: Arabs shaved the forelock of a pardoned captive as a sign that they had subdued and seized him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r10.anchor: وكانت العرب تجز ناصية الأسير الممنون عليه لتكون تلك علامة أنه قدر عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r11.claim: Dābba means every kind of animal; it is singled out because animals are the class addressed and spoken of.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r11.anchor: و «الدابة» : جميع الحيوان، وخص بالذكر إذ هو صنف المخاطبين والمتكلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p181/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p181/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p181/r1.claim: God’s actions are perfectly ordered, His speech truthful, and His promise true; the straight-path phrase means rectitude in everything attributed to Him, with an implied noun understood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p181/r1.anchor: يريد أن أفعال الله عز وجل هي في غاية الإحكام، وقوله الصدق، ووعده الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains that every creature is in God's grasp, possession, and dominion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة المعنى أنها في قبضته وملكه وسلطانه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r2.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head; seizing it means controlling and humbling the person's whole body.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r2.anchor: أن الناصية شعر مقدم الرأس فإذا أخذت بها من شخص فقد ملكت سائر بدنه وذل لك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid says God's path is the truth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r4.claim: Another reading supplies an omitted verb: God guides to a straight path.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r4.anchor: وقال غيره في الكلام إضمار تقديره إن ربي يدل على صراط مستقيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī offers one connection: since all remain in God's grasp, no fugitive can escape His path or any concealed thing evade Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنه لما أخبر أنه آخذ بنواصي الخلق كان معناه أنهم لا يخرجون عن قبضته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī's other connection is that, despite His power over them, God does not wrong them and intends only justice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p118#3/r6.anchor: والثاني أن المعنى أنه وإن كان قادرا عليهم فهو لايظلمهم ولايريد إلا العدل ذكرهما ابن الأنباري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r1.claim: Every creature is under God's dominion and control; He is a just judge who does not wrong anyone and is on a straight path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r1.anchor: تحت قهره وسلطانه، وهو الحاكم العادل الذي لا يجور في حكمه، فإنه على صراط مستقيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r2.speaker: أيفع بن عبد الكلاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r2.claim: A report from Aifa says God takes His servants by their forelocks and is more compassionate to the believer than a parent is to a child; the unbeliever is addressed in 82:6.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r2.anchor: عن أيفع بن عبد الكلاعي أنه قال في قوله تعالى: {ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم} قال: فيأخذ بنواصي عباده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r3.claim: God alone deserves exclusive worship: idols are inanimate, unable to benefit or harm, hear or see, or show loyalty or hostility, while all things are under His sovereignty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p330/r3.anchor: وقد تضمن هذا المقام حجة بالغة ودلالة قاطعة على صدق ما جاءهم به، وبطلان ما هم عليه من عبادة الأصنام

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r7.claim: The nasiya is the front hair of the head; another definition is the hairline at the forehead.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r7.anchor: والناصية: مقدم شعر الرأس، وقيل: هو قصاص الشعر

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r8.claim: The root of nasiya conveys connection, as in a desert tract that joins another and the verb for becoming connected to it.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r8.anchor: وأصل الناصية: الاتصال من قولهم: مفازة تناصي مفازة، أي: تتصل بها

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r9.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock is an expression for overpowering and possessing it.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r9.anchor: والأخذ بالناصية عبارة عن القهر والملك.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses God’s being on a straight path as His being upon the truth.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r2.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r2.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā glosses it as God’s sound and well-ordered governance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r2.anchor: على تدبير محكم , قاله علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r3.claim: A further possible sense is the path of the afterlife, where people return to God for recompense and final judgment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p477/r3.anchor: أنه على طريق الآخرة في مصيركم إليه للجزاء وفصل القضاء

MUJAHID:v1p305#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p305#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p305#4/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the straight path as the truth.
MUJAHID:v1p305#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ إن ربي على صراط مستقيم ﴾ يعني على الحق

MUQATIL:11:56-58/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r1.claim: Hud says he trusts God in response to their threat that their idols will harm him.
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r1.anchor: ربي وربكم } حين خوفوه آلهتهم أنها تصيبه

MUQATIL:11:56-58/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r2.claim: دابة means any creature or thing, and God taking its forelock means that He causes it to die.
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r2.anchor: يعني ما من شيء، { إلا } و { هو آخذ بناصيتها }

MUQATIL:11:56-58/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:56-58/r3.claim: God being on a straight path means that He is upon the truth.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r1.claim: God owns every creature and holds it under His power; His lordship over both parties grounds Hūd's trust.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r1.anchor: أى مالكها لما ذكر توكله على الله وثقته بحفظه وكلاءته من كيدهم وصفه بما يوجب التوكل عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r2.claim: Taking each creature by its forelock figuratively depicts God's possession and control.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r2.anchor: ومن كون كل دابة فى قبضته وملكته وتحت قهره وسلطانه والأخذ بالناصية تمثيل لذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r3.claim: This means either the Lord is upon truth and never deviates, or He guides to a straight path.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160#4/r3.anchor: إن ربى على الحق لا يعدل عنه أو إن ربى يدل على صراط مستقيم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r7.claim: Tawakkul here means accepting God’s judgment and trusting in His help.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r8.claim: Mā min dābba means any creature that moves on earth and is in the nominative position as the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r8.anchor: أي نفس تدب على الأرض وهو في موضع رفع بالابتداء.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r9.claim: God holds each creature’s forelock, directing it as He wills and preventing it from harming Hūd.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r9.anchor: أي يصرفها كيف يشاء، ويمنعها مما يشاء أي فلا تصلون إلى ضري.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r10.claim: Every living thing may be called dābb or dābba; the feminine ending is emphatic.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r10.anchor: وكل ما فيه روح يقال له داب ودابة والهاء للمبالغة.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r11.claim: Al-Farraʾ explains taking the forelock as owning the creature and having power over it.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r12.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r12.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains it as overpowering the creature, since one seized by the forelock is subdued.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r12.anchor: وقال القتبي: قاهرها لأن من أخذت بناصيته فقد قهرته.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r13.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak says God gives the creature life and then death; the meanings are close.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يحييها ثم يميتها والمعنى متقارب.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r14.claim: The nāṣiya is the hairline or forelock at the front of the head; naṣawtu means I stretched its forelock.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r14.anchor: والناصية قصاص الشعر في مقدم الرأس. ونصوت الرجل أنصوه نصوا أي مددت ناصيته.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r15.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r15.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the forelock is specified because Arabs use it as an idiom of submission; captors cut a prisoner’s forelock as a mark of triumph.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r15.anchor: قال ابن جريج: إنما خص الناصية لأن العرب تستعمل ذلك إذا وصفت إنسانا بالذلة والخضوع

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r16.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r16.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim interprets the verse as God having measured deeds before creation and placing the light of His prior knowledge in forelocks to drive creatures toward their decreed acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r16.anchor: وقال الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» قوله تعالى: { ما من دابة إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها } وجهه عندنا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r17.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s statement that God decreed all measures fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:54-56/r17.anchor: رواه عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r2.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim explains nāṣiya as the place where hidden deeds became manifest in the decrees, and says creatures’ motions were placed on their foreheads between the eyes.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r2.anchor: وإنما سميت ناصية لأن الأعمال قد نصت وبرزت من غيب الغيب فصارت منصوصة في المقادير

QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r3.claim: The author challenges al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim’s interpretation by citing the description of Abu Jahl’s forelock as lying and sinful, which the interpretation cannot explain.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas says ṣirāṭ is a clear way in Arabic; although God can do all things, He judges creatures only with justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: الصراط في اللغة المنهاج الواضح والمعنى أن الله جل ثناؤه وإن كان يقدر على كل شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r5.claim: Another explanation is that there is no flaw in God’s governance and no discrepancy in His creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:55-57/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا خلل في تدبيره، ولا تفاوت في خلقه سبحانه.

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r1.claim: Hud says neither his people nor their idols can harm him because he relies on God, the powerful owner of him and everything.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r1.anchor: يعني : إنكم وإلهتكم لا تقتدرون على ضرري فإني متوكل على الله القادر القوي وهو مالكي ومالك كل شيء

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r2.claim: The naṣiya is the forelock or the hair growing at the front of the head; taking it means overpowering and controlling its owner.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r2.anchor: الناصية عند العرب منبت الشعر في مقدمة الرأس ويسمى الشعر النابت هناك أيضا ناصية تسمية له باسم منبته

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r3.claim: Arab usage describes a submissive person as having his forelock in another's hand, since whoever holds it has mastery over him.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r3.anchor: والعرب إذا وصفوا إنسانا بالذلة والخضوع لرجل قالوا : ما ناصيته إلا بيد فلان ، أي : إنه مطيع له لأن كل من أخذت بناصيته

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r4.claim: Taking every creature by its forelock is a representative metaphor for God's effective power and complete control over creation.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r4.anchor: وأخذ الله بناصية الخلائق استعارة تمثيلية لنفاذ قدرته فيهم

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r5.claim: God owns every creature and disposes of it as He wills; even the mightiest creature is small beside His power and cannot resist His decree.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r5.anchor: والغرض من هذا الكلام الدلالة على عظمته وجلالة شأنه وكبرياء سلطانه وباهر قدرته وأن كل مقدور وإن عظم وجل في قوته وجثته فهو مستصغر

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r6.claim: God's rule rests on truth and justice: no wrongdoer escapes Him and no one who seeks His protection is lost.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r6.anchor: يعني : إنه على الحق والعدل في ملكه لا يفوته ظالم ولا يضيع عنده معتصم به.

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r7.claim: Every creature moving toward good or evil is seized by God and drawn toward either; all remain humbled in His power.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r7.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية ما من دابة تدب في طلب الخير والشر إلا هو آخذ بناصيتها يجرها بها إلى الخير والشر

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r8.claim: A seeker should pursue God by the straight road of the Sacred Law, walking the path of spiritual discipline to arrive at reality.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r8.anchor: من طلبه فليطلبه على صراط مستقيم الشريعة على أقدام الطريقة فإنه يصل إليه بالحقيقة

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r9.claim: The straight path is the one whose end is God alone, as the verse says that the final destination is to Him.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r9.anchor: وأيضا يعني : الصراط المستقيم هو الذي ينتهي إليه لا إلى غيره كقوله : وأن إلى ربك المنتهى}

BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r10.speaker: در نقد النصوص
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r10.claim: The cited work describes the divine essence as the source of all actions and effects, drawing each creature toward God according to its capacity; this is the secret of the forelock and straight path.
BURSEVI:v4p92#2/r10.anchor: ودرنقد النصوص قدس سر جامعه مذكور است درباب احديت افعال وبيان تأثيرات ومؤثرات كه آن ذات متعاليه كه في الحقيقة مصدر جميع أفعال

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r10.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r10.claim: Al-Azharī says nāṣiya denotes the hairline at the front of the head, and by extension the hair growing there.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r10.anchor: الناصية عند العرب منبت الشعر في مقدم الرأس ويسمى الشعر النابت هناك ناصية باسم منبته

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r11.claim: Taking someone by the forelock was an Arab idiom for subduing and controlling them; captors cut a released prisoner's forelock as a mark of having conquered him.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r11.anchor: لأن كل من أخذت بناصيته فقد قهرته

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r12.claim: The verse means every living creature is under God's might and power and submits to His decree.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r12.anchor: أي ما من حيوان إلا وهو تحت قهره وقدرته

RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r1.claim: One reading balances God's absolute power over creatures with justice: although able to rule them, He wrongs no one and acts only with right and fairness.
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r1.anchor: أنه وإن كان قادرا عليهم لكنه لا يظلمهم ولا يفعل بهم إلا ما هو الحق والعدل والصواب

RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila take God's holding every creature by its forelock as proof of unity, and His straight path as proof of justice; they say religion is completed by unity and justice.
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r2.anchor: قالت المعتزلة قوله : { ما من دابة إلا هو ءاخذ بناصيتها } يدل على التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r3.claim: A second explanation says no hidden thing escapes God's notice and no fugitive gets away: the straight path is the route no one can avoid.
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r3.anchor: ولا يفوته هارب ، فذكر الصراط المستقيم

RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p12/r4.claim: A third explanation takes the phrase to mean that the Lord guides or urges people toward the straight path through the call.
